summary: Automatic fallback to CPU-backed variant after capacity pressure causes p99 spikes and intermittent 504s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sharp increase in p99 latency for generation endpoints and intermittent 504 timeouts after midday traffic surge. Customer traffic was routed from their pinned GPU-backed variant to an automatic fallback variant that appears to be CPU-backed and required prolonged warmup.

Impact: Approximately 18% of Lexicon.ai requests (over a 30m window) experienced >2s p99 increased latency and ~3% resulted in 504 gateway timeouts. User-facing product degraded for multi-tenant workflows; customer is on Dedicated tier and expects predictable latency.

Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-lexicon-1) in us-east region. Traffic pattern: burst from 12:05–12:40 UTC with sustained 2x traffic above historical 95th percentile.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send sustained concurrent generation traffic matching their workload (batch of 20 concurrent streams, avg prompt length 280 tokens) against pinned model redwood-13b-quantized-v2.
2) Observe automatic routing policy kick in when preferred GPU variant reaches capacity.
3) Observe fallback path sends traffic to an alternate variant (reported as open-13b-lite) which shows long initialization and slow token throughput.

Observed behavior: Automatic fallback routed traffic to an initializing CPU-backed replica. The replica spent ~90s in initializing state with repeated kernel JIT/warmup logs. During that time, requests queued at the gateway, leading to 504s and elevated p99 for the rest of traffic. Dashboard traces show bursts of routing decisions where policy chose cost-saving variant under heavy load instead of temporarily increasing dedicated GPU burst capacity.

Expected behavior: Under capacity pressure, fallback routing should prefer low-latency warm alternatives or trigger burst capacity for Dedicated customers before selecting cold CPU-backed variants that require substantial warmup. Fallback to cold variants should be avoided for pinned Dedicated pools.

Temporary workaround applied: Support updated the customer's routing policy to pin a warm GPU-compatible variant and increased burst_capacity to prevent routing to CPU fallback. Applied at 12:58 UTC; customer reported p99 returned to baseline within 6 minutes.

Logs (excerpt):
[12:11:02] routing: route_decision: prefer_variant=open-13b-lite, reason=capacity_exhausted(pool=customer-dedicated-lexicon-1)
[12:11:04] serving-runtime: replica open-13b-lite-3 state=initializing, cache_miss=true, kv_cache_unavailable=true
[12:11:18] kernel: jit_compile:start model=open-13b-lite-3, duration=expensive
[12:12:35] api-gateway: proxy: request queued_wait=24s, upstream_timeout=30s -> 504

Timeline:
- 12:05 UTC - traffic surge detected
- 12:10 UTC - autoscaler hit max_gpu_replicas for pool
- 12:11 UTC - routing policy selected fallback variant open-13b-lite
- 12:11–12:50 UTC - large number of requests routed to initializing replicas
- 12:58 UTC - Support adjusted routing policy & increased burst capacity
- 13:04 UTC - metrics returned to baseline

Business impact: Customer SLA breach risk. Several production customers of Lexicon.ai reported degraded performance.

Additional notes: The fallback variant selected is flagged as compatible by the model catalog but lacks a warm image and precompiled kernels for this customer's typical sequence lengths. This appears to be a mismatch between routing policy preference and variant readiness metadata.

investigation_notes: Confirmed fallback-to-cpu variant decisions correlate with pool hitting max_gpu_replicas; autoscaler refused additional GPU replicas despite burst_capacity available due to quota check regression.

Routing ranker currently ranks variants by cost and compatibility flags but does not have a strong penalty for 'initializing' state or absence of precompiled kernels. This allowed a cheaper CPU variant to outrank warm GPU variants under heavy load.
Observed that model-catalog entries for open-13b-lite lack 'warm_image' and 'jit_ready' metadata; need to add readiness signals consumed by routing.
PR #512 (autoscaler quota refactor) introduced an edge-case where dedicated pools with burst_capacity were still blocked if pool_quota_remaining==0; reproducer created in staging.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Applied routing override for customer and increased burst_capacity to avoid CPU fallback. Verified metrics returned to baseline within 6 minutes.
Medium-term: Engineering to add readiness_score to model catalog and modify routing ranker to factor in readiness and warm_image presence. (Owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Fix autoscaler quota regression: rollback of PR #512 in progress and patch to respect burst_capacity when pool quota is exhausted. (Owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Follow-up: Offer SLA goodwill credit and share post-incident report with Lexicon.ai after root cause fix deployed. (Owner: CS Manager)
Postmortem links and tasks will be added to related_confluence_pages once complete.
